problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description: Find the two entries in an array that add up to a target. Each input has exactly one pair of distinct indices.
problems.input: The first line contains the integers in the array, separated by spaces. The second line contains the target.
problems.output: Print the two zero-based indices in ascending order.
constraints: Array values and the target are between −10⁹ and 10⁹.

samples.explanation: The two equal values are at different indices.

problems.title: Longest Unique Substring
problems.description: Find the length of the longest contiguous substring with no repeated characters.
problems.input: One line containing a lowercase string s.
problems.output: Print the maximum length.

problems.title: Palindrome Number
problems.description: Determine whether the usual decimal representation of an integer reads the same in both directions.
problems.input: One line containing an integer x.
problems.output: Print true or false in lowercase.
constraints: The minus sign is part of the representation.

samples.explanation: Reversing the representation moves the minus sign.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description: Determine whether each opening bracket is matched by a closing bracket of the same type, with brackets closed in the correct order.
problems.input: One line containing a string s made of (), [], and {} characters.
problems.output: Print true if the string is balanced, or false otherwise.

samples.explanation: The square bracket must close before the parenthesis.

problems.title: Furina’s Rounding
problems.description: Round an integer up to one significant digit. Find how much you would have to subtract from the rounded number to get the original number.
problems.input: One line containing a positive integer n.
problems.output: Print the rounded value minus n.
constraints: Use integer arithmetic. The rounded value may have an extra digit.

problems.title: Chess Piece Values
problems.description: Look up the value of a chess piece. A queen is worth 9, a rook 5, a bishop and knight 3 each, and a pawn 1. The king is priceless.
problems.input: One lowercase piece name: queen, rook, bishop, knight, pawn, or king.
problems.output: Print the value, or priceless for a king.
constraints: The input is always one of the six piece names.

problems.title: IB Grading
problems.description: Choose an answer key for a true/false exam to maximize the number of students who pass. A student passes when at least K answers match the key.
problems.input: The first line contains N, M, and K. Each of the next N lines contains a string of M binary digits representing one student’s answers.
problems.output: Print the maximum number of students who can pass under a single key.

samples.explanation: The key 10100 gives two students a perfect score.
The key 111 passes the first, third, and fourth students.

problems.title: Rock, Paper, Scissors
problems.description: You must play the same move every round. Find whether one choice lets you win strictly more rounds than you lose. Tied rounds do not count. Rock beats scissors, scissors beats paper, and paper beats rock.
problems.input: The first line contains N. Each of the next N lines contains the opponent’s move: rock, paper, or scissors.
problems.output: Print yes if a winning choice exists, or no otherwise.

samples.explanation: Paper wins twice, loses once, and ties once.
Every choice wins and loses once.

problems.title: Wand Selection
problems.description: Discard one occurrence of the largest measurement and compute the floor of the average of the remaining measurements.
problems.input: The first line contains N. The next N lines each contain one positive integer measurement.
problems.output: Print the average rounded down to an integer.

problems.title: Score Tally
problems.description: Count how many quiz scores meet or exceed the passing cutoff.
problems.input: The first line contains N and the cutoff K. The second line contains N scores.
problems.output: Print the number of scores greater than or equal to K.

problems.title: Word Frequency
problems.description: Find the most frequent word in a list. When frequencies tie, choose the word that comes first alphabetically.
problems.input: The first line contains N. The second line contains N space-separated lowercase words.
problems.output: Print the chosen word.
constraints: Each word has 1–20 lowercase English letters.

samples.explanation: graph and map both occur twice.

problems.title: Trail Totals
problems.description: Find the elevation change along each queried stretch of a hiking trail. Individual segments can go up or down.
problems.input: The first line contains N and Q. The second has N segment changes. Each of the next Q lines contains two one-based indices L and R.
problems.output: For each query print the sum from L through R, inclusive, on its own line.

problems.title: First Available
problems.description: For each request, find the first shelf whose capacity meets or exceeds the requested size. Shelf capacities are sorted in nondecreasing order.
problems.input: The first line contains N and Q. The second contains N sorted capacities. The third contains Q requested sizes.
problems.output: For each request, print the one-based index of the first suitable shelf, or −1 if none exists. Print one answer per line.

problems.title: Longest Study Streak
problems.description: A study log records completed days as 1 and missed days as 0. With up to K make-up days, find the longest contiguous streak you can complete.
problems.input: The first line contains N and K. The second contains N integers, each 0 or 1.
problems.output: Print the maximum length of a contiguous segment containing at most K zeroes.

problems.title: Room Bookings
problems.description: Choose as many nonoverlapping meeting requests as possible for a single room. A meeting may start at the exact time another ends.
problems.input: The first line contains N. The next N lines each contain a start and end time.
problems.output: Print the maximum number of meetings you can schedule.

problems.title: Island Survey
problems.description: Count islands in a map. Land cells that share an edge belong to the same island. Diagonal contact does not connect islands.
problems.input: The first line contains R and C. The next R lines contain C characters each: # for land and . for water.
problems.output: Print the number of islands.

problems.title: Campus Routes
problems.description: Find the fewest paths a student must walk to get from building 1 to building N. Each path connects two buildings in both directions.
problems.input: The first line contains N and M. Each of the next M lines contains the endpoints of a path.
problems.output: Print the fewest paths needed, or −1 if N cannot be reached.
constraints: Each endpoint is between 1 and N.

problems.title: Course Order
problems.description: Determine whether students can finish every course when each prerequisite course must be completed before its dependent course.
problems.input: The first line contains N and M. Each of the next M lines contains A and B, meaning course A must be finished before course B.
problems.output: Print yes if all courses can be completed, or no if the requirements contain a cycle.
constraints: Courses are numbered from 1 to N.

problems.title: Coin Workshop
problems.description: Make an exact total using the fewest coins. You have an unlimited supply of every listed denomination.
problems.input: The first line contains N and the target T. The second line contains N positive coin values.
problems.output: Print the fewest coins required, or −1 if the total is impossible.

problems.title: Delivery Network
problems.description: Find the cheapest route for a delivery from depot 1 to depot N. Each connection works in both directions and has a nonnegative cost.
problems.input: The first line contains N and M. Each of the next M lines contains U, V, and the cost W of traveling between them.
problems.output: Print the minimum total cost, or −1 if no route exists.

problems.title: Festival Lineup
problems.description: Keep as many floats as possible in a parade while their heights increase strictly. Floats that stay must keep their original relative order.
problems.input: The first line contains N. The second contains the N float heights in their original order.
problems.output: Print the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
